# Capability index

<!-- Generated by scripts/capabilities.py — do not edit by hand. -->

Every public name in `functax` (28 of them), each listed once at
its public home and grouped by the module that defines it, with the
first sentence of its docstring; then the public API of jax, equinox, lineax, einx. Search this page before
writing a helper: if what you need is here, compose it; if it is almost
here, extend it where it lives. Regenerate with `uv run poe capabilities`
after changing a public API (`tests/test_capabilities.py` checks it is
current).

## `functax`

| Name | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `FunctaxError` | class | Base class for every exception raised by ``functax``. |
| `GeometryError` | class | Raised when an axis, grid or point set is malformed. |
| `MissingExtraError` | class | Raised when a module needs the ``functax[jax]`` extra and it is missing. |
| `OutsideDomainError` | class | Raised under ``outside="raise"`` when a target lies outside the domain. |
| `PolicyError` | class | Raised when an interpolation policy names an option that does not exist. |
| `ValidationError` | class | Raised when an argument fails validation. |

## `functax.geometry`

### Affine raster maths on the array namespace of the input: pixels, centres, windows. (`functax._src.geometry._affine`)

| Name | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `from_pixel` | function | Map fractional pixel (row, col) to coordinates (x, y): the inverse of `to_pixel`. |
| `pixel_centres` | function | The x and y of every pixel centre of a grid, each of shape (rows, cols). |
| `to_pixel` | function | Map coordinates (x, y) to fractional pixel (row, col), centres at integers. |
| `window` | function | The row and column slices of the pixels that cover ``bounds``. |

### Pairwise distances between point sets, in the metric the point sets carry. (`functax._src.geometry._metric`)

| Name | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `pairwise_distance` | function | The distance from every source to every target, in their shared metric. |

### The sphere: lon/lat to unit vectors and back, and chord and geodesic distances. (`functax._src.geometry._sphere`)

| Name | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `chord_distance` | function | The straight-line distance through the sphere between every pair. |
| `geodesic_distance` | function | The great-circle distance between every pair. |
| `lonlat_to_unit` | function | Lift longitude and latitude onto the unit sphere. |
| `unit_to_lonlat` | function | Longitude and latitude of vectors on (or off) the unit sphere. |

### CRS-free geometry types: an axis, affine, rectilinear and curvilinear grids, points. (`functax._src.geometry._types`)

| Name | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `AffineGrid` | class | A regular 2-D grid given by an affine transform and a shape. |
| `Axis` | class | One strictly monotone coordinate axis, optionally periodic or in time. |
| `CurvilinearGrid` | class | A 2-D grid whose node coordinates are given per node, such as a swath. |
| `Metric` | type alias | Alias of `typing.Literal['euclidean', 'chord', 'geodesic']`. |
| `Points` | class | Scattered sites, with the metric their distances use. |
| `RectilinearGrid` | class | A tensor-product grid with one `Axis` per dimension. |

### Locate targets on an axis, and remap the taps that run off its ends. (`functax._src.interp._locate`)

|---|---|---|

| `locate` | function | The cell index i, the offset t ∈ [0, 1) and the inside flag of each target. |
| `remap_taps` | function | Bring tap indices back onto [0, N − 1] by a boundary rule. |

| Name | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `Policies` | class | Outside the domain, at missing samples, and at the edges. |

| Name | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `Readout` | class | c → f̂(X*): the read-out of a plan, from coefficients to target values. |
| `Stencil` | class | A sparse read-out H: row k reads S source values at flat indices. |

## Upstream: `lineax`

linear operators and solvers; the lineax view of every plan

### `lineax`

| Name | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `AbstractLinearOperator` | class | Abstract base class for all linear operators. |
| `AbstractLinearSolver` | class | Abstract base class for all linear solvers. |
| `AddLinearOperator` | class | A linear operator formed by adding two other linear operators together. |
| `AutoLinearSolver` | class | Automatically determines a good linear solver based on the structure of the operator. |
| `BiCGStab` | class | Biconjugate gradient stabilised method for linear systems. |
| `CG` | class | Conjugate gradient solver for linear systems. |
| `Cholesky` | class | Cholesky solver for linear systems. |
| `ComposedLinearOperator` | class | A linear operator formed by composing (matrix-multiplying) two other linear operators together. |
| `Diagonal` | class | Diagonal solver for linear systems. |
| `DiagonalLinearOperator` | class | A diagonal linear operator, e.g. for a diagonal matrix. |
| `DivLinearOperator` | class | A linear operator formed by dividing a linear operator by a scalar. |
| `FunctionLinearOperator` | class | Wraps a *linear* function `fn: X -> Y` into a linear operator. (So that `self.mv(x)` is defined by `self.mv(x) == fn(x)`.) |
| `GMRES` | class | GMRES solver for linear systems. |
| `IdentityLinearOperator` | class | Represents the identity transformation `X -> X`, where each `x in X` is some PyTree of floating-point JAX arrays. |
| `JacobianLinearOperator` | class | Given a function `fn: X -> Y`, and a point `x in X`, then this defines the linear operator (also a function `X -> Y`) given by the Jacobian `(d(fn)/dx)(x)`. |
| `LSMR` | class | LSMR solver for linear systems. |
| `LU` | class | LU solver for linear systems. |
| `MatrixLinearOperator` | class | Wraps a 2-dimensional JAX array into a linear operator. |
| `MulLinearOperator` | class | A linear operator formed by multiplying a linear operator by a scalar. |
| `NegLinearOperator` | class | A linear operator formed by computing the negative of a linear operator. |
| `Normal` | class | Wrapper for an inner solver of positive (semi)definite systems. |
| `NormalCG` | function | Deprecated helper function. |
| `PyTreeLinearOperator` | class | Represents a PyTree of floating-point JAX arrays as a linear operator. |
| `QR` | class | QR solver for linear systems. |
| `RESULTS` | class | An [enumeration](https://docs.kidger.site/equinox/api/enumerations/), with the following entries: |
| `SVD` | class | SVD solver for linear systems. |
| `Solution` | class | The solution to a linear solve. |
| `TaggedLinearOperator` | class | Wraps another linear operator and specifies that it has certain tags, e.g. representing symmetry. |
| `TangentLinearOperator` | class | Internal to lineax. |
| `Triangular` | class | Triangular solver for linear systems. |
| `Tridiagonal` | class | Tridiagonal solver for linear systems, uses the LAPACK/cusparse implementation of Gaussian elimination with partial pivotting (which increases stability). . |
| `TridiagonalLinearOperator` | class | As `lineax.MatrixLinearOperator`, but for specifically a tridiagonal matrix. |
| `conj` | function | Elementwise conjugate of a linear operator. |
| `diagonal` | function | Extracts the diagonal from a linear operator, and returns a vector. |
| `diagonal_tag` | constant | `diagonal_tag` |
| `has_unit_diagonal` | function | Returns whether an operator is marked as having unit diagonal. |
| `invert` | function | Returns a `lineax.FunctionLinearOperator` representing the (pseudo)inverse of `operator`. |
| `is_diagonal` | function | Returns whether an operator is marked as diagonal. |
| `is_lower_triangular` | function | Returns whether an operator is marked as lower triangular. |
| `is_negative_semidefinite` | function | Returns whether an operator is marked as negative semidefinite. |
| `is_positive_semidefinite` | function | Returns whether an operator is marked as positive semidefinite. |

| `linear_solve` | function | Solves a linear system. |

| `materialise` | function | Materialises a linear operator. |
| `negative_semidefinite_tag` | constant | `negative_semidefinite_tag` |

| `min` | function | Compute the minimum of values in the given tensor. |
| `minimum` | function | Compute the minimum of values of multiple given tensors. |
| `multiply` | function | Compute the product of values of multiple given tensors. |
| `not_equal` | function | Computes the non-equality comparison between values of two given tensors. |
| `prod` | function | Compute the product of values in the given tensor. |
| `rearrange` | function |  |
| `reduce` | function |  |
| `roll` | function | Rolls the elements in the given tensor by the specified shift amounts. |
| `set_at` | function | Sets values in a target tensor from an update tensor at the coordinates specified by an indexing tensor. |
| `softmax` | function | Compute the softmax of values in the given tensor. |
| `solve` | function | This function is an alias for :func:`einx.solve_axes`. |
| `solve_axes` | function | Solve for the length of all axes in an expression under the given constraints. |
| `solve_shapes` | function | Solve for the shapes of the einx expressions under the given constraints. |
| `sort` | function | Returns values in the given tensor sorted in ascending order. |
| `std` | function | Compute the standard deviation of values in the given tensor. |
| `subtract` | function | Computes the difference between values of two given tensors. |
| `subtract_at` | function | Subtracts values from a target tensor by an update tensor at the coordinates specified by an indexing tensor. |
| `sum` | function | Compute the sum of values in the given tensor. |
| `true_divide` | function | Computes the true division between values of two given tensors. |
| `var` | function | Compute the variance of values in the given tensor. |
| `vmap` | function |  |
| `vmap_with_axis` | function |  |
| `where` | function | Conditionally select values from two tensors based on a boolean mask. |
